Turn the parallelogram off true and exactness dies in your hand: the taut ruled line bows, the copy shears off the ghost, the badge goes red. Snap to f = 1 and it springs true. The parallelogram carries the proof — not the act of drawing.

The Bench

The Drawing Room

A four-bar that keeps its shape
copies your hand — exactly, ×s.
colophon — the estate-correction this bench makes

The fourth brass drawing-engine of the estate, kin to The Straightedge (an exact line), The Trammel (an ellipse), and The Spirograph (a rosette). This one copies your hand at a dialed scale.

The Straightedge's SPEC (linkage) once dropped a pantograph, reasoning its exact-affine claim (pen = O + s·(input − O)) was only reachable as a degenerate collinear rod — "a straight stick on screen." The cut conflated the collinearity THEOREM (O, T, P on a line) with the open-parallelogram FORM. A real four-bar keeps all four bars at non-zero extent — the parallelogram open forever (apex height ≥ 1.66 here) — yet, SOLVED from the dragged tracer, P = O + s·(T − O) holds to machine-ε. Here it is, drawn by hand.

The sole pantograph authority is pantograph/core.mjs (DOM-free, pure), forge-inlined byte-for-byte between the sentinels on this page and proved by a headless Node twin: collinearity area < 1e-12 from the closed-form RR-solve · |OP|/|OT| ≡ s against an independent affine oracle · all four bars hold to machine-ε while the master-figure apex height stays > 1.66 · and the detune knob is the falsifiable neg-control — every wrong bar length bows the line and shears the copy off the ghost. The page runs the inlined copy; the pill reruns the same self-test the twin proves.
